title: Pitch vs Tempo: What to Change for Music Practice
description: Pitch changes how high or low notes sound; tempo changes how fast the beat moves.
direct: Change pitch when the notes sit too high or low for you. Change tempo when you need more time to play the same passage.
figureAlt: Guitar and metronome distinguish pitch, or note height, from tempo, or beat speed.

cards.choice.heading: Choose the change you need
cards.choice.body: A song that is too high calls for a pitch adjustment. A passage that is too fast calls for a tempo adjustment. Changing one does not mean the other must change.
sections.explain.heading: Why voices can sound unnatural
sections.explain.body: A mixed recording contains voices, instruments and transients together. Processing the complete mix can change vocal character or introduce audible artifacts. A pitch tool is not proof of formant correction, vocal separation or studio-quality transposition. Those advanced capabilities are not claimed here.
sections.practice.heading: Keep a useful reference
sections.practice.body: The iPhone app lists pitch and tempo changes for practice in its current iPhone release. Export tools require Pro. Use a normal-speed original alongside the practice copy so you can check the intended rhythm. Streaming-service playback is not the same as an importable audio file; use an accessible local source.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Should I change both settings at once?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Start with the one that solves the problem. Compare the same short phrase with the original before making a second change.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Which version should I use before rehearsal?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Return to the original speed to check phrasing and timing. If you rehearse in a different key, use a pitch-adjusted copy and confirm its key with your instrument.
